CHR_01.reason: Clear microgranular or hyaline-appearing calcareous wall structure visible under light microscopy.

CHR_02.reason: Overall test outline in the section is rounded/ovoid.

CHR_03.reason: Septa separating chambers are clearly visible throughout the coils.

CHR_04.reason: Numerous chambers arranged in multiple whorls are visible.

CHR_05.reason: Coiling pattern does not fit standard uniserial/biserial/triserial categories; appears spirally coiled with complex turns.

CHR_06.reason: Coils shift axis during growth, characteristic of streptospiral arrangement.

CHR_07.reason: Inner whorls are oriented at angles to outer whorls, indicating changing coiling planes.

CHR_08.reason: Later whorls envelop earlier ones completely.

CHR_09.reason: No major ontogenetic shift from coiled to uncoiled serial chambers.

CHR_10.reason: Presence of multiple internal partitions and chamber subdivisions indicating structural complexity.

CHR_11.reason: Secondary subdivisions or chamberlets are visible within the peripheral chambers.

CHR_12.reason: Central proloculus region appears as a simple initial chamber.

CHR_13.reason: Subepidermal partitions or beam-and-rafter-like network visible along the outer wall.

CHR_14.reason: No distinct central pillars are observed in this section.

CHR_15.reason: No lateral chamberlets observed along the flanks.

CHR_16.reason: Apertures are not clearly intersected or visible in this plane of section.

CHR_17.reason: No marginal cord structure is discernible.

CHR_18.reason: Surface septal filaments not visible in internal thin section view.

CHR_19.reason: Entire isolated test is surrounded by matrix, showing no attachment surface.

CHR_20.reason: Insufficient comparative section data to determine dimorphism conclusively.

CHR_21.reason: The section cuts the test at an angle to the main coiling axes, showing shifting internal whorls.
